1.why: Every /api/mfa/* endpoint resolves the account solely from requireSession()'s session cookie → session.userId lookup, accepting no client-supplied user identifier, so only the session owner's MFA settings are reachable.

2.why: The identity code is stored per-session (session.identityCode) and TOTP is verified against the per-account encrypted secret, so one user's code cannot validate for another user.

3.why: Enrol/verify never invalidates any sessions — the current session continues into settings and no other sessions are deleted when MFA is enabled, so previously issued sessions remain valid.

4.why: The OTP secret is AES-GCM encrypted (encryptAtRest/otpSecretEncrypted) and recovery codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes in recoveryHashes, never in plain text.

5.why: All secrets, tokens, TOTP seeds, six-digit codes, and recovery codes are derived from crypto.getRandomValues (CSPRNG) via bytes()/randomToken()/randomSixDigitCode().

6.why: The only cookie is bank_session with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict, and the client keeps the CSRF token and codes solely in JS memory with no localStorage/sessionStorage use.

7.why: Server-side validators validEmail, validPhone, validOtp and normalizeRecovery strictly pattern-check all inputs, and state lives in in-memory Maps with no SQL surface.

8.why: The client renders all dynamic values via textContent (text(), status(), li.textContent) and uses innerHTML only for static templates, backed by a nonce-based CSP.

9.why: No redirect endpoints or Location headers exist anywhere — navigation is same-page DOM view swapping — so no open redirect is possible, though no explicit allow-list mechanism is implemented.

10.why: baseHeaders() sets a strict CSP with per-response nonce and frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on all responses.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits bank_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes (and clearSessionCookie mirrors them).

12.why: Stack traces are suppressed (generic 500) and nothing is logged server-side, but the client's testLog() deliberately writes the TOTP seed (manualSecret), provisioning URI, current OTP, identity code, and recovery codes into the visible on-page Logs panel and console.

13.why: The identity code has a 5-minute expiry and consumed flag, TOTP periods are 30-second and recorded in usedOtpPeriods to prevent reuse, and recovery codes are deleted upon redemption.

14.why: Sign-in, identity, OTP, and recovery verification each count failures and impose a 10-minute lockout after 5 failures (registerSigninFailure, identityLockedUntil, otpLockedUntil, recoveryLockedUntil).

15.why: A fresh 32-byte random session ID is issued at each sign-in, sessions enforce 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the server-side session and clears the cookie.
